title: ₹20 Crore, a 90-Second Audio Clip, and the Voice That Haunts Bollywood's Biggest Director
excerpt: The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has sent Rohit Shetty a new extortion threat — and the message is chilling: the February shooting at his Juhu home was just 'the trailer.'
body:
On Saturday morning, someone on Rohit Shetty's staff pressed play on an audio clip that had arrived overnight. Ninety seconds later, the message was clear: pay ₹20 crore, or the man who built Bollywood's most lucrative action franchise becomes the target himself.

The voice on the clip is believed to belong to Shubham Lonkar, a close associate of jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi and a wanted suspect in the 2024 murder of NCP leader Baba Siddiqui. Mumbai Crime Branch has confirmed receiving the audio from Shetty's team and has sent it for forensic analysis. Juhu Police have registered a case.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=0J-nektQaeU

> "The firing at Rohit Shetty's house was only a trailer. If he does not pay, this time the bullets will be directed at the filmmaker himself."

That line, reportedly from the audio clip, carries a grotesque irony. Rohit Shetty — the director of the Singham franchise, the Golmaal series, and the sprawling Cop Universe that has generated thousands of crores at the box office — is now living inside the kind of scene he once choreographed for the screen. Only this time, there is no cut, no stunt double, no slow-motion hero walk through the flames.

The February Shooting

This is not the first time. On the night of February 1, 2026, five rounds were fired outside Shetty's Juhu residence near Hasya Kalakar Mehmood Chowk. The shooter, Deepak Sharma, arrived on a motorcycle and was later arrested in Agra. The Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility immediately.

The Mumbai Crime Branch filed a 1,624-page charge sheet in April, naming 15 accused. Two — Pravin Lonkar and Aarzo Bishnoi — remain absconders. The investigation revealed a well-organised operation stretching across state lines, with handlers coordinating from behind bars.

Saturday's audio clip represents an escalation: a direct, named demand with a specific price tag, delivered not through intermediaries but through the filmmaker's own staff.

An Industry Under Siege

Shetty is far from the only Bollywood figure in the Bishnoi gang's crosshairs. Salman Khan has lived under Y-plus security since the 2024 firing at Galaxy Apartments — and is now reportedly building an entirely new six-storey sea-facing bungalow in Bandra's Chimbai area, just minutes from the apartment where his family has lived since 1974. That balcony where he once waved to thousands of fans on Eid? Sealed.

Ranveer Singh has also received threats. Real estate developers, politicians, and industrialists across Maharashtra have reported similar extortion attempts using the Bishnoi gang's name — some genuine, some copycat. The pattern is consistent: audio clips, WhatsApp messages, six- and seven-figure demands.

For the Indian diaspora watching from abroad, the optics are stark. The men who make India's biggest, boldest, most triumphant cinema — the films that pack out theatres in New Jersey, Hounslow, and Brampton — are privately navigating a security crisis that no blockbuster budget can fix.

What Happens Next

Shetty has remained publicly silent since the threat surfaced. His next directorial, the much-anticipated Singham Again, is in advanced stages of post-production. He is also set to return as the host of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15.

Mumbai Police are treating the threat with urgency. The forensic analysis of the audio clip will determine whether the voice conclusively matches Lonkar's. In the meantime, security around Shetty has been visibly tightened.

But the larger question lingers like a scene that refuses to end: when does Bollywood's biggest action hero stop directing the danger and start being defined by it?

The trailer, it seems, is over. And nobody in the industry is laughing.
